trust_decision.summary: The reverse proxy decides which client IP to put in the outbound X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP. It does this in the Rewrite hook of newPortProxy: client-supplied trusted headers are stripped, then the value is rebuilt from RemoteAddr, or from the inbound XFF when RemoteAddr is loopback.

landing_point.why: This is the only httputil.ReverseProxy in the repo, and SetXForwarded plus the X-Forwarded-For override sit here. The strip list in internal/consts is the obvious place to add the header.

fix_sites.entry_point: any HTTP request to a proxied HTTP/HTTPS port (newPortProxy Rewrite via internal/proxymanager/proxy.go:540)
resolvePeerIP called from the same Rewrite hook
fix_sites.module_kind: helper in the same file (constant rename only)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Inbound XFF is trusted when RemoteAddr is loopback. A solver could argue this is the documented trust boundary for the Tailscale VIP-services hop (internal/proxyproviders/tailscale/services_server.go:672-674) and so leave it alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: For the VIP/services loopback hop, the backend must still get the real peer IP taken from the single inbound XFF value. An over-broad fix that always uses RemoteAddr would send 127.0.0.1 and break this (and the X-Forwarded-Proto https override next to it).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Copy the client's X-Forwarded-Proto/X-Forwarded-Host from r.In instead of deriving them from config.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The maintainer already overrides X-Forwarded-Proto by hand here because of a TLS-termination quirk. Copying the inbound value for 'behind another proxy' setups is a plausible feature change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second copy of the XFF peer-IP resolver (trustedPeerIP) used for Whois identity. A weakened copy (e.g. taking the first comma element) would be a how-type parser differential.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is already duplicated from resolvePeerIP (internal/proxymanager/port.go:592-610) in another package. The two copies drift easily.

O9_family: CWE-74 header injection / client-IP spoofing via X-Forwarded-For

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add X-Forwarded-For to consts.TrustedProxyHeaders (which is exactly the published fix).

out_of_scope_notes: internal/core/admin.go:72-134 grants a localhost/trusted-source admin bypass based on RemoteAddr. It is a separate protection and was not pursued.
internal/proxyproviders/tailscale/services_server.go:675-709 trusts XFF on loopback for Whois identity. It is the identity-lookup sink, not the proxied-header sink.
unverified: Main concern: Go's httputil.ReverseProxy, when Rewrite is set, already deletes Forwarded/X-Forwarded-For/-Host/-Proto from the outbound request before calling Rewrite. SetXForwarded only reads r.Out's prior XFF. So at the pinned commit (port.go:105,143) a client's XFF probably never reached the backend, and the published fix (fix.diff:26) is likely a no-op. The added regression test (fix.diff:80-151) would then probably pass before the fix too. This is from memory of the stdlib; I did not run anything.
Spoofing through the loopback-hop branch (port.go:593-609) is unchanged by the fix. Whether an untrusted client can reach the proxy port with a loopback RemoteAddr was not determined.
